title: Unmarked Line
subtitle: Gas Strike, Trench Collapse & Adjacent Structures

brief.userPrompt: A Wednesday in mid-April 2027, 0.6 inch of rain overnight. At 06:45 foreman and competent person Tomas Reyes inspected the trench at stations 14+00 to 18+00 (13 feet deep, 10-by-20-foot trench box, Type C soil, seepage noted at 16+00) and cleared work. The exercise starts at 09:45 with Site Superintendent Marcus Hale, Safety Director Priya Venkataraman and about 70 workers on site; crack gauges CG-1 to CG-3 on the Harlan & Weir print shop read 0.03, 0.05 and 0.09 inch (alarm 0.12, action 0.25). At 10:12 excavator E-7 (operator Gordon Pruitt) tears an unmarked gas service line at station 16+00 (the drawings show it, the field marks did not); gas hisses and smells in the trench; at 10:14 the 4-inch main pressure is at 55 psi upstream. At 10:20, while crews move out and the superintendent calls Valley Gas, the south trench wall at 16+05 slumps and shifts the trench box; pipe layer Luis Marquez is buried to the chest and a second worker climbs out injured. Pressure points: stop work and who has the authority; 911 with no street address (cross streets only); whether to evacuate the print shop (14 employees), the apartment house (9 residents), the church hall preschool (22 children, 4 staff) and the day-care play yard before the fire department arrives; rescuers must not dig in an unstable, gassed trench; the exclusion zone and the 300-foot gas standoff; crack gauge CG-3 passes the 0.12 inch alarm at 10:24 and the 0.25 inch action level at 11:05 as vibration and dewatering continue; whether the Engineer of Record Helen Brandvold, PE, can be reached and what she allows (shoring, shutting the dewatering pump); extrication at 12:10 and transport; Marquez is pronounced dead at the trauma center at 13:20, starting the OSHA 8-hour fatality clock (a second worker's hospitalization has its own 24-hour clock; the clock starts when a supervisor learned of it, not when the Safety Director did); notice to the owner's representative Joseph Albrecht within an hour and the written report within 5 working days; the insurer claims line and surety; notifying the Marquez family in person before any name is released; a local TV helicopter and a bystander's video post at 10:50 saying 'sewer workers buried, gas everywhere'; the Dayton building official's decision on the print shop; evidence preservation; and the restart conditions. The SimCell plays 911 and Dayton Fire Rescue 2, the battalion chief, Valley Gas, the OSHA area office, the building official Fiona Castellanos, the owner's representative, the insurer, the media and neighbors.
audience: Engineer of Record (advisor to the team)
constraints: Every email address of Larkspur uses the exercise domain larkspurconstructors.example; the owner uses stillwatersewer.example; outside parties use fictional domains; never a real agency, company or newspaper domain.

Placards and building status are written as words (INSPECTED, RESTRICTED USE, UNSAFE), never a color alone; the competent person, superintendent or Safety Director stops work, the Engineer of Record decides structural adequacy and only the building official declares a building unsafe; OSHA clocks are 8 hours (fatality) and 24 hours (hospitalization); every product is marked as an exercise.
Player roles are only those in the audience list; Dayton Fire Rescue, 911, the utilities, OSHA, the building official, the owner, the insurer, reporters and neighbors are played by the SimCell.

overview.theme: Who stops work and who decides, a rescue the contractor must not attempt, protecting neighbors before responders arrive, and speaking to families and the public before the facts are complete.
overview.threat: On a Wednesday in mid-April 2027, 0.6 inch of rain fell overnight. At 06:45 competent person Tomas Reyes inspected and cleared the 13-foot trench at stations 14+00 to 18+00 of the Stillwater Creek Interceptor. The trench uses a 10-by-20-foot trench box in Type C soil, and he noted seepage at 16+00. At 10:12 excavator E-7, run by operator Gordon Pruitt, tears a gas service line at station 16+00. The drawings show this line, but the field marks did not. Gas pours into the trench, and at 10:14 the 4-inch main upstream reads 55 psi. At 10:20 the south trench wall at 16+05 slumps and shifts the trench box. Pipe layer Luis Marquez is buried to the chest and a second worker climbs out injured. Vibration and dewatering continue to work on the Harlan & Weir print shop foundation 18 feet away. Crack gauge CG-3 passes its 0.12-inch alarm level at 10:24 and its 0.25-inch action level at 11:05.
overview.operationalImpact: All excavation stops. About 70 workers must move upwind and at least 300 feet from the gas. Engines within 100 feet shut down, and radios cannot be keyed in the gas area. This leaves foremen, laborers, ironworkers, crane operators and signal persons calling headcounts by voice while the buried pipe layer is out of reach. Larkspur crews must not dig into an unstable, gassed trench. The superintendent calls 911 with only cross streets to give, then waits for Dayton Fire Department Rescue 2 and a battalion chief to take command. He then hands them the shoring drawings, the soil classification record and the locate tickets. The shores, the spare trench box and the standby excavator in the east staging yard sit unused until the Incident Commander asks for them. Next door, the team must decide before the fire department arrives whether to evacuate the print shop (14 employees), the four-unit apartment house (about 9 residents), the Ninth Street Church hall preschool (22 children, 4 staff) and the Little Acorn Learning play yard. The church hall preschool's own muster point is in the gas standoff. Every 15 minutes the trailer dashboard shows CG-3 rising, against a print shop wall that already had a crack. When it reaches the action level, the building must be evacuated until the Engineer of Record and the Dayton building official decide. Only the building official can post the building INSPECTED, RESTRICTED USE or UNSAFE, which leaves owners and tenants waiting to learn if they can return. A local TV helicopter circles overhead. At 10:50 a bystander posts a video saying "sewer workers buried, gas everywhere," and calls start reaching the community hotline and the families. Extrication is at 12:10. The pipe layer is pronounced dead at the trauma center at 13:20, which starts the OSHA 8-hour fatality clock. The second worker's hospitalization has its own 24-hour clock, which starts when a supervisor first learned of it. The family must be told in person before any name is released.

objectives.name: Decision Making
objectives.text: Demonstrate the ability to stop all excavation, move about 70 workers upwind and at least 300 feet from the gas, and decide before Dayton Fire arrives whether to evacuate the print shop, the apartment house, the church hall preschool and the Little Acorn play yard, including choosing a new muster point outside the gas standoff.

objectives.name: Use of Doctrine
objectives.text: Demonstrate the ability to follow LC-EAP-01 section 4 by keeping Larkspur crews out of the failed, gassed trench, handing the shoring drawings, soil classification record and locate tickets to the Rescue 2 Incident Commander, and committing the standby shores, spare trench box and excavator only when the Incident Commander asks for them on the Engineer of Record's advice.

objectives.name: Technical Analysis
objectives.text: Demonstrate the ability to read crack gauge CG-3 at its 0.12-inch alarm and 0.25-inch action levels against the print shop foundation, notify the Dayton Division of Building Inspection under LPONRC section 3, and keep the print shop evacuated until the Engineer of Record and the building official decide, without Larkspur declaring any building INSPECTED, RESTRICTED USE or UNSAFE.

objectives.name: Communication
objectives.text: Demonstrate the ability to run the LPONRC section 2 call sequence and the OSHA 8-hour fatality and 24-hour hospitalization clocks, tell the pipe layer's family in person before any name is released, and issue a holding statement through the Project Executive only, after the owner's representative is told, that answers the bystander video without guessing at the cause.

roles.name: Site Superintendent
roles.description: Manages the site from the gas strike until responders arrive: stops work, places the 911 and call-tree calls, orders neighbors out and serves as site liaison to the Rescue 2 Incident Commander.
standingOrders: Life First: call 911 and the gas utility together, then clear the trench edge and shut down engines. Nobody goes into the failed trench to dig.
Neighbors Before Responders: if gas, CG-3 or the collapse threatens an adjacent building, order the occupants out now and pass the evacuation to the fire department when units arrive.

Hand Over, Don't Command: give the Incident Commander the shoring drawings, soil record and locate tickets, and commit the shores, trench box and standby excavator only when the Incident Commander asks.

roles.name: Safety Director
roles.description: Owns stop-work authority, the OSHA and building-official notifications, the incident log, scene preservation and the in-person family notification.
standingOrders: Clock Discipline: the OSHA clocks start when any Larkspur supervisor learns of the event. Log that time, report the fatality within 8 hours and the hospitalization within 24 hours, even when schedule pressure is high.
Preserve the Scene: move nothing except to save a life. Keep the shoring, soil logs, daily inspection forms and CG-3 data exactly as they are, and take photos only after responders release the scene.
Family Before Public: tell the family in person with the foreman and the Project Executive before any name is released.

roles.name: Project Manager
roles.description: Manages the project-side response: owner notice, the written incident log kept by the PM's assistant, subcontractor coordination and the schedule and cost consequences of the stop.
standingOrders: Notify on Time: the owner's representative hears within 1 hour, and the written contract notice goes out within 24 hours, whatever the schedule pressure.
Stop Means Stop: the job stays shut until the Safety Director and the Engineer of Record agree it can restart. Do not trade schedule against an unresolved hazard.
Document Everything: make sure the call log records who was called, when and what they ordered.

roles.name: Project Executive (spokesperson)
roles.description: Owns the company response and is the only Larkspur voice to media, insurer and surety, speaking only after the owner's representative has been told.
standingOrders: One Voice: no other Larkspur employee speaks to media. Say what is known, what is not known and what is being done, and never guess at the cause.
Truth Over Reassurance: the viral video and the helicopter will push for fast answers. Do not confirm names, the death or the cause until the facts and the family allow it.
Owner First: tell the owner's representative before any public statement, and have the District's PIO approve anything that names the District.

roles.name: Competent Person (foreman)
roles.description: Manages the trench work area: inspects for hazards, removes workers from danger, takes the voice headcount and keeps people and vibration away from the failed trench.
standingOrders: Clear the Hazard: get every worker out of the trench and away from the edge, keep trucks back 50 feet and do not key radios in the gas area.
Count by Voice: confirm a full headcount from every foreman and report who is missing to the superintendent.
Own the Record: the 06:45 inspection and the seepage noted at 16+00 must stay exactly as written. Do not change or add to the form.

roles.name: Engineer of Record (advisor to the team)
roles.team: Team F: Engineer of Record (advisor to the team)
roles.description: Manages structural advice to the team: the trench protective system, any shoring the Incident Commander requests, and the CG-3 readings on the print shop foundation.
standingOrders: Data Before Opinion: read CG-3 against its 0.12-inch alarm and 0.25-inch action levels with the time of each reading, and do not dismiss the existing crack.
Advise, Don't Declare: give a structural opinion on the print shop, but only the building official can post it INSPECTED, RESTRICTED USE or UNSAFE.
Shore on Request: design or approve shoring only when the Incident Commander asks for it.

phases.title: The Unmarked Line
phases.goal: Tests whether the team acts on early warnings, stops all excavation at the gas strike under LC-EAP-01 section 6 and LETPS section 9, and decides before Dayton Fire arrives whether to evacuate the neighbors. This phase holds the first of the exercise's decision points.
beats: (09:45) Normal shift at stations 14+00 to 18+00 after 0.6 inch of overnight rain. The 06:45 LC-F-22 by Tomas Reyes noted seepage at 16+00. Cascade Dewatering reports that the 12-inch pump at sump 15+20 is struggling to keep up. The utility drawings show a service connection at 16+00 that the field marks for locate ticket 2711-4482 do not show (LSUAP section 4, LETPS section 6). Will anyone stop machine digging inside 18 inches?

(09:58) Noise item: a Pike & Marlow Paving truck is waiting at the east gate (Ninth Street and the rail spur), and Hollis Electric asks the superintendent about a lockout. Neither matters, but both take the superintendent's attention.

(10:12) Gordon Pruitt's excavator E-7 tears the gas service at 16+00, and at 10:14 the 4-inch Valley Gas main reads 55 psi. LC-EAP-01 section 3 and section 6 apply: 'All stop' on radio channel 2, then no radios keyed in the gas area. About 70 workers move upwind at least 300 feet, and engines within 100 feet shut down. The 911 call can give only the cross streets Corliss Avenue and Ninth Street. Players must also call the Valley Gas emergency number and Ohio811.

(10:20) The south wall at 16+05 slumps and shifts the trench box. Luis Marquez is buried to the chest, and a second worker climbs out hurt. Foremen take headcounts by voice against the sign-in board. Does anyone try a crew rescue in the gassed, failed trench, which LC-EAP-01 section 4 does not allow?

(10:24–10:35) DECISION POINT: CG-3 on the trailer 2 dashboard passes its 0.12-inch alarm level against the print shop wall, which already had a crack. Before Rescue 2 arrives, the team must decide whether to evacuate the Harlan & Weir print shop (14 employees), the four-unit apartment house (about 9 residents), the Ninth Street Church hall preschool (22 children, 4 staff) and the Little Acorn play yard. Evacuating clears out vulnerable neighbors on Larkspur's own authority. Waiting leaves them in the gas area. The preschool's muster point is inside the 300-foot standoff, so a new one must be chosen.

phases.title: Command Passes to Fire
phases.goal: Tests whether the team hands command to the Rescue 2 battalion chief, holds its own resources until they are requested, and reads CG-3 to its action level without declaring any building status.
beats: (10:45) Time jump: the Rescue 2 battalion chief holds command and asks for the shoring drawings, the soil classification record (LETPS section 3, Type C) and locate ticket 2711-4482. The standby shores, the spare trench box and the standby excavator in the east staging yard stay unused. A Larkspur foreman pushes to 'just bring the excavator over.'

(10:50) A bystander video saying 'sewer workers buried, gas everywhere' spreads. A local TV helicopter circles, and the community hotline and family phones start ringing. A reporter calls the Project Executive and sets a noon deadline.

Red herring that splits the room: a print shop manager says the wall crack 'was always there.' A crew member blames the rain, not the strike, for the collapse. Players must rely on the CG-3 trend and the LC-F-22 record and not guess at a cause.

(11:05) The 15-minute dashboard update shows CG-3 past its 0.25-inch action level. LETPS section 7 requires the print shop to be evacuated and the Dayton Division of Building Inspection to be notified under LPONRC section 3. Larkspur must not call the building INSPECTED, RESTRICTED USE or UNSAFE. The Engineer of Record advises the team.

Valley Gas says its crew will 'squeeze off the service within 30 minutes,' but the crew is still not on scene at 11:40. Meanwhile the team works through the LPONRC section 2 call sequence (Project Manager, Safety Director, owner's representative at stillwatersewer.example).

phases.title: Extrication and Families
phases.goal: Tests the team's support to the rescue, its handling of families and the public, and its start of the hospitalization reporting clock.
beats: (11:50) The Incident Commander asks for the spare trench box and the shores on the Engineer of Record's advice. Larkspur sends equipment and operators only at the Incident Commander's direction. The Engineer of Record warns about the 12 kV Miami River Power duct bank crossing at 17+20 near where the box would be placed.

(12:10) Luis Marquez is extricated and transported to the trauma center. The hospital confirms the second worker is formally admitted. The Safety Director must fix when a supervisor first learned of the admission, because the OSHA 24-hour clock runs from that moment.
Families arrive at the west gate and call the hotline. LPONRC section 4 applies: a quiet place, a named liaison, and no names released before next of kin are told in person.

(12:20) Under media pressure with the reporter's deadline already passed, the Project Executive issues a holding statement of under 150 words after the owner's representative is told. It must say what is known, what is not known and what is being done, and give the next update time. It must answer the bystander video without guessing at the cause.
The Dayton building official's inspector arrives at the print shop. Owners and apartment residents want to know when they can go back in. Only the building official can post a placard.

phases.title: Fatality and Restart Hold
phases.goal: Tests the reporting after the fatality, the in-person family notification, and the conditions under LETPS section 9 before any work restarts, leading to ENDEX.
beats: (12:50) Valley Gas reports the service squeezed off and the gas cleared, and the Incident Commander shrinks the standoff. Things come back in order: gates reopen, engines restart outside the trench zone and radios are keyed again. The excavation stays stopped.

Hurdle: the next CG-3 reading is still moving, and the 16+00 service needs a replacement part that Valley Gas says is days away. Neither the apartment house gas nor the print shop can be restored yet. The building official posts the print shop RESTRICTED USE pending the Engineer of Record's assessment, and the tenants push back.

(13:20) Luis Marquez is pronounced dead at the trauma center, which starts the OSHA 8-hour fatality clock. The Project Manager and Safety Director arrange to tell the family in person before any name is released. A reporter has learned the name from social media.

Verification before restart: the superintendent drafts the written release, but it needs the Safety Director's agreement, the Engineer of Record's agreement on the protective system, and a new LC-F-22 by Tomas Reyes or Imani Duclos after the utility strike. Pressure from the owner's representative about the schedule is to be expected.

(13:35) Notifications are confirmed: OSHA fatality report, the 24-hour hospitalization report, the Ohio811 damage report and the insurer. The Project Executive issues an updated statement. The team writes the after-action note on the gap between the drawings and the marks at 16+00. ENDEX at 13:45.

objectiveCapabilities.why: The superintendent has to stop all excavation, account for about 70 workers and move them, call 911, and order the neighboring buildings out before Dayton Fire arrives. That means running the LC-EAP-01 first-five-minutes and adjacent-building steps on Larkspur's own authority, then handing the evacuation to Fire when units arrive.

A buried pipe layer is a technical rescue. LC-EAP-01 section 4 keeps Larkspur crews out of the trench, makes the superintendent the liaison who hands over the drawings, the soil record and the locate tickets, and holds the standby shores, trench box and excavator until the Incident Commander asks for them.

Command passes from Larkspur to the Rescue 2 Incident Commander. The team has to work inside that single command and keep the LC-EAP-01 section 2 stop-work and restart authority while crews press to act on their own.

The Engineer of Record and the superintendent read the CG-3 trend against the LETPS section 7 alarm and action levels and keep the data log unaltered. The Safety Director tells the building official, who alone decides the print shop's status.

The Project Executive is the only voice. She speaks only after the owner's representative has been told, issues known/unknown/being-done holding statements without guessing at cause, and gets the District PIO's approval for anything naming the District under LPONRC section 4.

The team has to run the OSHA 8-hour fatality and 24-hour hospitalization clocks from the moment any supervisor learned of the event, and tell the pipe layer's family in person before any name is released.

hotwash.methodDescription: Ask the room for three things that went well and three that broke or failed during the response, with honest answers getting the same weight as the wins. Go around the room team by team (site supervision, safety, engineering, Project Executive and communications), write each item on the whiteboard in two columns, and don't debate anything until all six items are up.

questions.text: At I-01, before the strike, you had two warnings within 90 seconds. Cascade reported the sump up 8 inches and losing to the south wall at 16+00. Your field engineer then showed you a service tee on the Valley Gas drawing that wasn't marked on locate ticket 2711-4482, with E-7 about 10 feet away. LSUAP 4 already notes that the field marks didn't show the 16+00 service. When did you stop trusting the paint and start trusting the drawing? Who had the authority to stop E-7 at that moment, and did anyone use it? Did you treat the mismatch as a hazard that stops the work, or as a ticket problem to raise with the one-call center later?

At I-07b the laborer foreman asked for the standby excavator keys, and two laborers were pulling on gloves to go into a trench reading 18% LEL. Who stopped them, what exactly was said, and was it the superintendent, the competent person or the fire department? Under LC-EAP-01 section 4, Larkspur crews stay out of a failed, gassed trench. Did the room hold that line as a rule, or did it feel like a choice you were arguing about? What would have kept the crew from reaching that point, for example being told what Rescue 2 was doing and why?

CG-3 on the Harlan & Weir foundation passed its 0.12-inch alarm level at 10:24 and its 0.25-inch action level at 11:05. Walk us through what changed at each threshold. Who told the Engineer of Record and who called the Dayton Division of Building Inspection, and at what time? Under LETPS 7, all excavation and dewatering effects in the zone of influence are the issue, and the building stays evacuated until the EOR and the building official say otherwise. Did anyone on our side start to say the print shop was 'fine' or 'safe to re-enter'? Did the readings go into the incident log the way LPONRC 5 requires, with the data left unaltered?

At I-07 you faced a viral video claiming a 'clearly marked' gas line and several workers buried, 19 hotline calls including three possible relatives, and a Dayton Ledger reporter asking for names and the number dead by noon. What did you actually say to the public and to the relatives before you knew the facts? Who spoke: the Project Executive only, or others too? Was the owner's representative told first? Who was assigned to tell the pipe layer's family in person? When did the OSHA 8-hour and 24-hour clocks start, and who was tracking them?

At I-12 the battalion chief asked for your spare box, your shores, crane C-2 and the crew to run it. The EOR would not approve tracking the crawler over the 12 kV Miami River Power duct bank at 17+20. That left two choices: wait about 45 minutes for the utility to de-energize, or take 35 to 40 minutes walking around by the west end. Meanwhile, water was rising about an inch every 5 minutes. When did you first call Miami River Power and Valley Gas: at the strike, or only when the crane route forced the question? Did you commit equipment only when the Incident Commander asked for it, based on the EOR's advice? What could you have prepared before 11:50, such as a crane route, a mat design or a de-energization request, so this decision took minutes instead of three-quarters of an hour?

simcellScripts.rolePlayed: Valley Gas Company emergency dispatcher and crew foreman, with the Ohio811 damage desk; speaks also for the dependent customers (Harlan & Weir print shop and the apartment house owner) who lose gas service
simcellScripts.trigger: A player calls Valley Gas or Ohio811 to report the strike at 16+00 (from I-02 onward), asks for an ETA (I-10), or asks when service is restored to the neighbors (I-17).
hardQuestions: "Main or service? Give me the exact address and cross street. 'The trench on Ninth' doesn't get a truck dispatched."

"What's your locate ticket number? 2711-4482? Is that service on your ticket response? Your field marks didn't show it? Then why was a machine digging that close? Have you opened a damage report with Ohio811 yet?"
"Is anyone in the gas area? Have you shut down engines and moved people upwind? Has anyone from your side touched a valve on our main? Don't. That's ours."
(Neighbors, after I-17) "No gas until Monday means no heat and no hot water. Who's paying for the hotel for the tenant with the baby, and who's paying for my lost $40,000 job? Put it in writing."
concessions: Gives a dispatch reference number and a firm crew ETA only after the caller supplies the address, the locate ticket number, and confirms 911 has been called and nobody is touching the main.

Ohio811 issues damage report DR-27-0414-0397 against ticket 2711-4482 only after the superintendent reports that the service was on the drawings but unmarked, and that digging has stopped and the line is protected (LETPS 6, step 4).
The neighbors accept a named Larkspur contact, a written note of the Monday tee repair date, and a referral to the insurer claim. They do not accept a verbal 'you'll be home by two.'

simcellScripts.rolePlayed: Dayton 911 dispatcher, then the Dayton Fire Department Rescue 2 battalion chief (Ninth Street Command)
simcellScripts.trigger: The superintendent calls 911 after the collapse (I-03), or any player approaches the Command table, asks to send Larkspur workers or equipment into the trench, or offers the staged shores, trench box or crane (I-06, I-07b, I-10, I-12).
hardQuestions: (911) "What's the address? 'Corliss and Ninth' — which corner, which gate do my units enter? How many trapped, how deep, is gas still leaking? Is anyone from your crew in that trench right now? Get them out."
(Battalion chief) "Who's my one Larkspur liaison? I want the shoring drawings, the soil classification record and the locate ticket in my hand, not 'they're in the trailer somewhere.'"
"I've got two of your laborers pulling on gloves by the excavator. Are they yours to control or mine? If one goes past my tape, I've got three people to rescue."
"Your engineer says the crane can't cross 17+20. So what's your fastest legal route, how long, and who's the lift director? I need a number, not a debate."
concessions: Gives the Larkspur liaison a place beside Command and real-time status only after one named liaison shows up with the shoring drawings, soil classification record and locate ticket 2711-4482.

Requests Larkspur's spare 10-by-20 box, hydraulic shores, crane and lift director only after gas reads safe and the EOR has given a route. Accepts the west-end walk-around or a utility de-energization over an unapproved crossing of the duct bank.
Shrinks the standoff to a 50-foot tape and lets gates, engines and radios resume, but only after Valley Gas reports 0% LEL. Keeps the trench as an investigation scene until he releases it.

simcellScripts.rolePlayed: OSHA area office duty officer (Cincinnati area office covering Dayton)
simcellScripts.trigger: The Safety Director or any player calls OSHA to report the in-patient hospitalization (after I-13) or the fatality (after I-18), or OSHA calls back at I-19.
hardQuestions: "Employer name, site address, time of the event, number of employees affected, and a contact. And what time did any supervisor or manager first learn of this? Not you, anyone in supervision."

"Your foreman got the hospital call at 11:25 and the admission was at 11:20? Then your 24-hour clock started at 11:25. Was it a formal in-patient admission or an observation stay? Do you have that from the hospital?"
"The worker who was buried, was he your employee or a sub's? Who is the controlling employer on this site? Has the sub been notified, and is that written down?"
"Is the trench box, the shoring, the soil log and your daily inspection form for today still exactly as found? Has anyone added anything to that form since 06:45?"
concessions: Logs the report and gives a report reference number only when the caller can state the employer, location, time, number affected, contact, and the time a supervisor first learned (LPONRC 3).

Accepts the fatality report as timely if it is within 8 hours of 13:24. Schedules the compliance officer for about 15:00 and says it will accept the records as preserved: form LC-F-22 unaltered, the locate ticket, the CG-3 log and the incident log (LPONRC 5).
Notes cooperation favorably if Larkspur volunteers the subcontractor notification record and a written timeline.

simcellScripts.rolePlayed: City of Dayton Division of Building Inspection on-call inspector, acting for building official Fiona Castellanos (937-555-0170)
simcellScripts.trigger: The Safety Director or EOR calls the building official when CG-3 passes its alarm level (I-04) or action level (I-08), or when adjacent buildings are evacuated. Or a player asks the inspector to post or clear a building (I-15, I-17).
hardQuestions: "Which buildings did you evacuate, at what time, and on whose order? Why am I hearing about the action level from the news and not from you?"
"Give me CG-3 with times, every reading since 09:45. What's the unit, where's the sensor, and is anything still vibrating or dewatering next to that wall right now?"
"Where is your Engineer of Record's written opinion on that south foundation? A phone call is not an assessment."
"Your gate guard told the apartment owner 'probably by two.' Who authorized that? Only the building official decides re-entry. Stop promising times."
concessions: Posts the print shop RESTRICTED USE (not INSPECTED) only after receiving the timed CG-3 readings and a verbal EOR opinion. Will consider changing the posting after the EOR's written assessment arrives.

Allows escorted entry to the print shop office to retrieve essential items. Allows re-occupancy of the apartment house and church hall once gas is controlled, provided Larkspur confirms no further monitoring action levels on those buildings.
Agrees to a set time for the next re-evaluation if Larkspur commits to logging CG-3 every 15 minutes and sending the readings.

simcellScripts.rolePlayed: Marisa Kline, reporter, Dayton Ledger (fictional), 937-555-0147; also covers the Channel 9 Miami Valley News assignment desk calls
simcellScripts.trigger: The Project Executive returns or takes a media call (I-05, I-07, I-14, I-18b), or any Larkspur player other than the PE talks to a reporter or photographer at the gate.
hardQuestions: "I'm told two workers are dead and your crew hit a gas line that was clearly marked. Confirm the number and the names. I file at noon, with or without you."
"Channel 9's chyron says '2 WORKERS DEAD.' Is that right or not? If you won't say, I write 'Larkspur declined to comment' again."
"I have the name off Facebook and a scanner listener says the trauma center called off its alert. Did he die? Channel 9 leads with the name at 2. On the record: was that line marked or not?"

assumptions: The exercise is held in a no-fault learning environment. It evaluates plans, procedures and decisions, not individual players, subcontractors or any real structure.
The scenario is plausible, and events occur as they are presented. Players accept the site conditions, the wind, the gauge readings and the responder arrival times without debating them.

Players respond in accordance with existing plans, policies and procedures, including LC-EAP-01, the LSUAP and the notification list. Where a plan is silent, players say what they would do and note the gap for the hot wash.

Players speak only for their own role and authority as LC-EAP-01 section 2 assigns it. Decisions that belong to Dayton Fire, Valley Gas, OSHA or the City of Dayton building official are requested from the SimCell, not assumed.
Players know only what the current module and the injects tell them. They do not act on information from later modules.
artificialities: There are time jumps between modules: 10:45, 11:45 and 12:45. Players are told the events in between on facilitator time-jump cards, not in real time.

The SimCell plays everyone outside the room. That includes Dayton Fire Rescue 2 and Ninth Street Command, Valley Gas, Miami River Power, Cascade Dewatering, Pike & Marlow, Hollis Electric, the owner's representative and District PIO, the neighbors and the preschool, the trauma center, OSHA, Ohio811, the insurer, the City building inspector, the media and families.

Systems are named as they appear in the plans but are not touched. Nobody operates or reads the radios on channels 1 and 2, the trailer 2 crack gauge display, the community hotline, the gas valves or any equipment.

Injects are delivered on paper or screen. This includes radio calls, phone calls, alarms, emails, social media posts and news articles. All media outlets, posts and the readings for named buildings are fictional and are marked EXERCISE.

**Module 1 — "The Unmarked Line" (09:45–10:45)**

It is 09:45 on Wednesday, April 14, 2027, at the Stillwater Creek Interceptor Phase 2, east of downtown Dayton. It is overcast and 52°F. A light wind is blowing from the west-southwest at about 8 mph, and the ground is saturated after 0.6 inch of rain overnight. About 70 workers are on site: Larkspur crews plus Pike & Marlow Paving, Hollis Electric and Cascade Dewatering.

The pipe crew is laying 48-inch pipe in the 13-foot trench at stations 14+00 to 18+00. They are working from the 10-by-20-foot trench box in Type C soil. Excavator E-7 (operator Gordon Pruitt) is digging ahead of the box toward 16+00. At 06:45, competent person Tomas Reyes signed form LC-F-22 clearing the trench, with one note: "seepage, south wall, 16+00."

The trailer 2 monitoring display shows the Harlan & Weir print shop crack gauges at CG-1 0.03 in, CG-2 0.05 in and CG-3 0.09 in. The alarm level is 0.12 in and the action level is 0.25 in. The Site Superintendent and Safety Director are on site. Status: normal.

**Module 2 — "Command Passes to Fire" (10:45–11:45)**

It is 10:45. At 09:55, Cascade reported that the 15+20 sump was gaining on its pump, with water coming through the south wall near 16+00. The field engineer found a service tee at 16+00 on the Valley Gas drawing that had no paint on the ground. At 10:12, E-7 tore a plastic gas line at 16+00. The main reads 55 psi, and the wind is carrying gas east toward the trailers and Ninth Street.

At 10:20, the south wall let go at 16+05 and shoved the box over a foot. Luis Marquez is buried to the chest and still talking. The E-7 operator's helper climbed out with a broken, bleeding forearm and left by ambulance. The pipe crew count first came up 2 short. At 10:24, CG-3 passed its alarm level at 0.13 in. The preschool director and the print shop manager asked whether to go or stay, Channel 9 wanted numbers by 10:50, and the owner's representative emailed asking what was happening.

Dayton Fire Engine 12 and Rescue 2 arrived at 10:38. The battalion chief has set up Ninth Street Command at the west gate and holds command. Fire units have taken over the neighbor evacuation Larkspur started. Rescue 2 will not enter the trench while gas is hissing, and Valley Gas is not yet on scene. Water has reached Luis Marquez's waist. The chief wants one Larkspur liaison beside him, plus the shoring drawings, the soil classification record and locate ticket 2711-4482. Nobody from Larkspur goes past his tape. The standby shores, spare trench box and standby excavator sit unused in the east staging yard.

**Module 3 — "Extrication and Families" (11:45–12:45)**

It is 11:45. Over the past hour, Larkspur laborers pushed to take the standby excavator and go in with shovels. CG-3 passed its action level at 11:05 and read 0.26 in. Six print shop employees briefly went back in to shut down the presses. The owner's representative demanded answers within 15 minutes and asked that nothing naming the District go out without her approval. The print shop manager insisted the gauge was only measuring an old crack. A laborer asked the competent person to add a line to the 06:45 LC-F-22. Valley Gas pushed back its arrival and told Larkspur not to touch any valves. The chief said he may want the staged shores and spare box once the gas is controlled.

The Valley Gas truck arrived at 11:43, and its crew is hand-digging at 16+00. Gas can still be heard. Luis Marquez has been buried for 85 minutes, the water is above his waist, and medics are passing him a warming blanket and oxygen. The E-7 operator's helper left by ambulance for the regional trauma center at 10:52.

The hotline has taken 34 calls. Cars are parking on Corliss Avenue, and people are walking toward the west gate asking for 'the boss.' The Dayton Ledger's noon deadline is 15 minutes away, and the Channel 9 helicopter is overhead. CG-3 has held at 0.26 in since 11:05. The print shop, the apartment house and the church hall preschool stay empty under fire department control.

modules.narrativeMd:
**Module 4 — "Fatality and Restart Hold" (12:45–13:45)**

It is 12:45. Rescue 2 got Luis Marquez out at 12:10. He was conscious, with crush injuries to both legs and hypothermia. He reached the regional trauma center at 12:31 and is in the trauma bay. The hospital has told Larkspur nothing more. At 12:12 the pipe crew foreman told the Safety Director that the trauma center had called his cell at 11:25. The charge nurse confirmed that the helper was formally admitted to orthopedics at 11:20 and that he is now in surgery.

The rescue moved the original box about 2 feet. The battalion chief has declared the trench at 14+00 to 18+00 an investigation scene, and nobody touches the box, the shores or the spoil. At 12:04 the Dayton Ledger ran 'TWO FEARED DEAD,' saying Larkspur declined to comment, and Channel 9 is airing '2 WORKERS DEAD.' The District PIO wants to see any statement before it goes out.

At 12:30 the City building inspector asked for the CG-3 readings with times and for the Engineer of Record's opinion. The print shop owner pressed for an INSPECTED sign. Valley Gas has almost finished squeezing off the service, and the hiss is faint. About 70 workers have been held at the musters for two and a half hours, and subcontractors want to send their people home. The hotline is at 52 calls. Fourteen family members, including Luis Marquez's wife, are in trailer 4, out of the cameras' view. The neighbors' buildings are still empty, Little Acorn is keeping its children indoors, and the owner's representative has emailed twice more.

Answering 'was the line marked?' on the record without guessing at the cause
